newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOTORCYCLING-JAPANESE VIE TO BEAT WORLD CHAMPION DOOHAN.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-JAPANESE VIE TO BEAT WORLD CHAMPION DOOHAN.

text.p: Reigning 500cc champion Michael Doohan will be seeking his second Grand Prix win of the season on Sunday on a track he hates.
The Australian Honda rider, who won the season opening race last week in Malaysia, is also anticipating tough competition from local riders on the fast Suzuka circuit in central Japan.
"Japan is not entirely one of my favourite race tracks and the Japanese are very hard to beat in Japan," Doohan told reporters.
Heading the local challenge is Norifumi Abe who won the Japanese Grand Prix here last year.
"I want to compete for the top. I know all those in 500cc are fast, but I keep telling myself I can do it," Abe said.
"It (Suzuka) is going to be a very important race for me."
The 21-year-old Yamaha rider clocked the fastest time of two minutes 09.089 seconds for the 5.864 km (3.644 mile) Suzuka track last year.
Other Japanese challengers include Tadayuki Okada, who won pole position but finished 10th in the Malaysian Grand Prix, and Nobuatsu Aoki who was third.
The Suzuka track frequently produces close finishes with its long straights and sweeping corners offering ample opportunities for overtaking.
